claims.text: High-entropy alloys are typically composed of at least five elements, each at roughly 5–35 atomic percent.
The proposed approach is applicable across the compositional space typical of high-entropy alloys.

Enhanced free-energy sampling coupled with HEA-tailored machine-learned interatomic potentials can determine melting temperature, fusion enthalpy and entropy, melting volume change, and liquid thermodynamic properties.
Interface pinning or metadynamics can be coupled with machine-learned interatomic potentials for high-entropy alloys.
Enhanced sampling elucidates the free-energy barrier between solid and liquid phases.
HEA-tailored machine-learned potentials accurately capture complex interatomic forces in multicomponent systems.
Enhanced sampling rigorously converges free-energy differences at the melting transition.
Converged free-energy sampling resolves subtle latent-heat and volume changes at melting.
Machine-learned potentials provide computational efficiency and accuracy over a vast HEA compositional space by parameterizing interatomic interactions.
The proposed method will predict melting temperatures with errors below ±30 K.
The proposed method will predict fusion enthalpy and entropy within a few percent error.
The proposed method will accurately estimate melting volume changes and liquid-phase properties across diverse HEA compositions.
Traditional DSC, CALPHAD, and standard atomistic simulations offer lower resolution and incur high computational cost when extended across HEA compositional complexity.
The method is applicable to multiple-principal-element alloys under near-equilibrium, high-temperature conditions.
Excessive compositional inhomogeneity or nonequilibrium behavior may place a system outside the method's effective range.
Machine-learned-potential transferability and free-energy convergence in highly disordered liquids are potential sources of uncertainty.
WTaMoNbV is a refractory high-entropy alloy that can serve as a validation system.
Failure to meet the target errors for melting temperature and fusion properties in multiple HEA compositions would falsify the proposed approach.

contradictions.description: The experimental design describes applying the method to a single well-characterized HEA, whereas the falsification rule requires failures in multiple HEA compositions. The stated design alone therefore cannot trigger the stated rule.
